subject: Novamed AWS Private Offer: commitment sprint, procurement lane & evaluation roadmap
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dawson <alex.dawson@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Novamed AWS Private Offer: commitment sprint, procurement lane & evaluation roadmap

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together an initial commitment sprint and procurement lane that maps the AWS Private Offer flow to the procurement tasks you outlined. Attached is a one-page MAP (20260915-Novamed-MAP-v1.xlsx) and a short AWS Private Offer checklist (AWS-Private-Offer-steps.pdf).

High level ask: can your procurement team confirm the target PO approval date so we can align offer activation and billing?

Key milestones (draft):
- Week 1 (Sep 15–Sep 21): Legal kickoff — exchange redlines; Redwood to provide standard SOW and SOC2 summary.
- Week 2 (Sep 22–Sep 28): Procurement validation — PO creation + internal approvals; Redwood prepares AWS Private Offer draft and pricing commitment.
- Week 3 (Sep 29–Oct 5): AWS Private Offer activation & test billing in partner account; verification of invoice routing to NovaMed finance.
- Week 4 (Oct 6–Oct 12): Production activation; start of committed capacity and first billing cycle.

Evaluation plan (concurrent):
- 2-week proof-of-concept (PoC) for the image-analysis pipeline with a capped sandbox spend.
- Shared eval prompts and latency targets documented in the MAP; Redwood will ship a pre-provisioned test instance.
- Quality checkpoints: sample outputs on day 3 and day 10.

Dependencies from NovaMed:
- Procurement PO target date (single date, please)
- Technical contact for AWS account and billing owner
- Legal point-of-contact for contract redlines
Open items for Redwood (we'll cover internally): pricing floor for private offer, 30/60/90 usage ramp, and whether you need consolidated AWS billing or direct Redwood invoice (we recommend AWS-managed billing via the marketplace for simplicity).

Attachments: SOC2-summary-Novamed.pdf contains the control summary we discussed. I can escalate a SOC2 artifact package if your audit team needs it.

If that draft looks good I’ll circulate the version to procurement and loop in Karthik for marketplace activation.

Best,

— Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Dawson <alex.dawson@novamed.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novamed.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novamed AWS Private Offer: commitment sprint, procurement lane & evaluation roadmap

Thanks Soojin — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Procurement target: our finance committee meets Sep 28 and we expect a PO to be issued by Oct 1 if legal redlines are minor. If there are major changes it may slip to Oct 8.
2) Billing: we prefer AWS-managed billing via Marketplace (so costs show on our AWS invoice). That aligns with internal chargeback.
3) Evaluation: 2-week PoC timeline works but we need sandbox credentials and a non-production billing cap (can your team set a hard cap?).

I’ll get the procurement POC and legal contacts over today. Lastly — can you confirm whether the private offer can be scoped to a committed monthly minimum or must it be an annual commit?

— Alex
VP Product, NovaMed Health
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Novamed AWS Private Offer: commitment sprint, procurement lane & evaluation roadmap

Forwarding Alex's note. Quick internal take: we can support both monthly committed minimum and annual committed tiers — the private offer SKU can be configured either way, but annual commit needs approval from Pricing (I can fast-track). For PoC cap, ops can enforce a hard spend cap in the test account.

Action items for us:
- Karthik: draft private-offer SKU options (monthly commit vs annual) and pricing examples.
- Laura: prep a short note for legal that outlines typical redline responses (payment terms, indemnity, data handling).

Ben
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Novamed AWS Private Offer: commitment sprint, procurement lane & evaluation roadmap

Following up with the SKU/options matrix. Draft notes: 
- Option A (Monthly commit): minimum monthly $10k, rolling monthly billing via AWS Marketplace, 30-day cancellation. Good for teams that want flexibility.
- Option B (Annual commit): $100k annual commitment, 12-month term, discounted effective rate (~18% off). Requires commit confirmation and PO at activation.
- PoC mode: sandbox account with hard spend cap enforced (we use AWS IAM budget alerts + instance-level quotas). We will provide a pre-provisioned test instance and a short onboarding playbook.

I attached a sample pricing table to the MAP. Will sync with Ben on final numbers.

-Karthik
Product Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dawson <alex.dawson@novamed.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novamed AWS Private Offer: commitment sprint, procurement lane & evaluation roadmap

Alex — thanks for the timeline confirmation. Per your note that PO may land by Oct 1, I updated the MAP to reflect two paths (fast path Oct 1 activation, contingency path Oct 8). Key updates in the attached MAP:

- Legal exchange window shortened to 3 business days for fast path (we'll triage redlines).
- AWS Private Offer activation checklist includes: Marketplace listing draft, accepted private offer in your AWS account, billing owner verified.
- Finance routing: if you choose AWS-managed billing we will send offer to the Marketplace account and AWS will invoice NovaMed directly. If you need Redwood invoicing we can enable that but requires a PO + separate billing agreement.

Next steps from NovaMed (requested):
1) Procurement: confirm target PO date (Oct 1 or Oct 8).
2) Legal: email redlines to laura@redwood.com by Sep 24 to keep fast path.
3) Tech: shared test AWS account id and billing owner contact for sandbox provisioning.

I’ve also initiated a DocuSign envelope for the standard SOW template (link below). If procurement prefers we can pause DocuSign until redlines land.

DocuSign: https://app.redwood.com/docusign/evt-987654
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/12345

Best,
— Soojin
From: Alex Dawson <alex.dawson@novamed.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novamed AWS Private Offer: commitment sprint, procurement lane & evaluation roadmap

Appreciate the update — fast path it is. Procurement will aim for PO on Oct 1. Legal (I've looped in Maria Chen) will send redlines by end of day Sep 24. Tech contact: I'll send AWS account id and billing owner tomorrow.

A few final asks before we lock: can Redwood confirm our PoC cap will be enforced and whether sample invoices can be produced during activation so our finance team can see the routing? Also please include a brief note in the MAP about data residency controls for the test instance.

If you can confirm those items, we’ll proceed with the fast path and target Oct 1 activation.

Thanks — Alex
--- End of thread ---
